paper_id: Sun et al. - 2008 - RCT A distributed tree for supporting efficient range and multi-attribute queries in grid computing
title: RCT: A distributed tree for supporting efficient range and multi-attribute queries in grid computing
motivation: Grid systems with millions of resources treat all resources equally without categorizing, forcing full-overlay traversal for queries
problem_framing: Resource discovery with two challenges: (1) efficiency without full traversal, (2) support for range and multi-attribute queries on categorized resources
key_insight: Categorize resources by primary attributes matching application requirements; use balanced AVL tree preserving locality; higher nodes don't bear more load
method_signature: RCT (Resource Category Tree): distributed AVL overlay with primary attribute ranges, load-aware adaptation, fault tolerance
evaluation_criteria: Query load per node, average search length (ASL), standard deviation of query load across HR nodes
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Parallel search uses stale range info when nodes adapt; fallback to sequential Algorithm 4; no mechanism for frequent HR updates
evidence_for_taste: higher-level nodes...not required to maintain more information
average search length will be less than that of complete BST
ASL with RCT is between 8.5 and 9
merge of light-loaded HRs will lead to higher efficiency
thinking_moves: Binary search tree structure applied to distributed resource categorization, borrowing well-known balanced tree properties
Identify practical DHT weakness (locality destruction) to justify non-DHT approach
Systematic query taxonomy: four types from two dimensions (range vs point, single vs multi-attribute)
Load thresholds define system states: light/warning/over to trigger adaptation (engineering heuristic)
Analyze worst/best case search bounds mathematically before empirical validation
Claim novelty through categorizing mechanism, not just indexing structure
